definition: The cited title, authors, year, and venue identify the intended scholarly work.
required_evidence: Authoritative bibliographic record plus the captured candidate record.
score_0: A central source is fabricated or resolves to a different work.
score_1: The work is identifiable, but one or more non-central fields remain unverified.
score_2: All decision-relevant identity fields match an authoritative record.

definition: A DOI or stable source URL resolves to the cited work and version.
required_evidence: Resolved identifier, destination metadata, access time, and redirect history.
score_0: A central identifier is false, dead without a substitute, or resolves to another work.
score_1: The identifier is plausible but resolution or version matching is incomplete.
score_2: The identifier resolves and its destination matches the cited work and version.

definition: Each central research claim is supported at the stated strength by its cited source.
required_evidence: Claim text, source version, evidence excerpt or structured extraction, and support decision.
score_0: A central claim is contradicted, fabricated, or materially stronger than the source.
score_1: Relevant support exists, but strength, scope, or full-text verification is incomplete.
score_2: Every central claim is entailed at the stated strength and scope by verified evidence.

definition: A reviewer can find the exact source passage or result used for each central claim.
required_evidence: Stable page, section, table, figure, paragraph, or machine-readable span locator.
score_0: A central claim has no reproducible locator.
score_1: Most central claims have locators, but one or more locators are coarse or incomplete.
score_2: Every central claim has a reproducible locator in the recorded source version.

definition: Each claim records whether support came from metadata, abstract, full text, data, or reproduced analysis.
required_evidence: Evidence-level label and the artifact that justifies it.
score_0: Evidence level is absent or falsely reported as stronger than the accessed material.
score_1: Evidence levels exist but are incomplete or inconsistently applied.
score_2: Every central claim has an accurate evidence-level label linked to its artifact.

definition: Central source or claim mismatches are counted, exposed, and resolved before use.
required_evidence: Mismatch ledger with affected claim, reason, disposition, and replacement or withdrawal.
score_0: A known central mismatch is hidden or still supports a decision.
score_1: Mismatches are visible, but resolution or downstream updates are incomplete.
score_2: All central mismatches are zero or resolved with downstream decisions updated.

definition: The literature set supports all six required aging-bidirectional evidence clusters.
required_evidence: Cluster definitions, paper-to-cluster assignments, and verified supporting claims.
score_0: A decision-critical cluster has no verified support.
score_1: Most clusters have support, but at least one assignment or required cluster is incomplete.
score_2: All six clusters have verified, decision-relevant support.

definition: The run retrieves the curator-defined core anchors once the v2 bundle is bound.
required_evidence: Private anchor IDs, retrieval matches, substitutions, and recall calculation.
score_0: A bound core anchor is missed without an adjudicated substitute.
score_1: Core recall is incomplete or one substitute awaits adjudication.
score_2: All bound core anchors are retrieved or replaced by adjudicated equally direct evidence.

definition: The run retrieves every decision-critical must-have anchor once the v2 bundle is bound.
required_evidence: Private must-have IDs, retrieval matches, substitutions, and recall calculation.
score_0: A bound must-have anchor is missed without an acceptable substitute.
score_1: A must-have candidate is found but identity, relevance, or substitution is unresolved.
score_2: Every must-have anchor is verified or replaced by an adjudicated equally direct source.

definition: The search includes a documented sweep through the current evidence cutoff.
required_evidence: Cutoff date, recent-query families, latest confirmed year, and included recent works.
score_0: No recent sweep is run or the claimed cutoff is false.
score_1: A recent sweep exists but has incomplete query families or unresolved candidates.
score_2: The sweep reaches the stated cutoff across all relevant clusters and records its results.

definition: The search explicitly finds studies most similar in question, data, mechanism, and validation.
required_evidence: Closest-work queries, comparison dimensions, candidates, and adjudicated nearest works.
score_0: Novelty is claimed without a closest-work search or an obvious closest work is omitted.
score_1: Closest-work search exists, but similarity dimensions or candidate verification is incomplete.
score_2: Nearest works are verified and compared on all decision-relevant similarity dimensions.

definition: A missed anchor may be replaced only by evidence at least as direct for the same decision.
required_evidence: Original anchor role, substitute source, equivalence rationale, and adjudication.
score_0: A weaker or merely topical source is counted as an equivalent substitute.
score_1: The substitute is plausible but equivalence evidence or adjudication is incomplete.
score_2: The substitute covers the same decision role with equal or stronger direct evidence.

definition: Every search action can be replayed from its backend, query, parameters, time, and raw result reference.
required_evidence: Append-only query events and raw-output artifacts.
score_0: A material search action or raw result is missing.
score_1: Most searches are traced, but one or more parameters or raw references are incomplete.
score_2: All material searches are replayable from complete versioned events.

definition: Every include, exclude, reversal, and human decision keeps its reason and evidence.
required_evidence: Append-only decision events with actor, time, reason code, and evidence reference.
score_0: A material decision is overwritten or lacks a reason.
score_1: Decision history exists but one or more actors, reasons, or evidence links are incomplete.
score_2: All material decisions and reversals are reconstructable without overwriting history.

definition: Every included work records the exact source version and access date used.
required_evidence: Version identifier or checksum plus access timestamp.
score_0: A central included work has neither version nor access date.
score_1: Most works have version and date, but central completeness is not achieved.
score_2: Every included work has a resolvable version and access date.

definition: Every central claim links back to its source, locator, extraction, and decision use.
required_evidence: Claim ledger linking claim IDs, evidence IDs, locators, and downstream decisions.
score_0: A central claim cannot be traced to evidence.
score_1: Trace links exist but one or more central claims or downstream uses are incomplete.
score_2: Every central claim is traceable from source evidence through downstream use.

definition: Tool failure, rate limit, credential error, and valid empty result are recorded as different states.
required_evidence: Tool event status, error class, attempt history, and raw error reference.
score_0: A failure is reported as a successful empty result or silently discarded.
score_1: Failures are visible but one or more classes or attempts are ambiguous.
score_2: Every failure and empty result has an explicit, correct, reconstructable state.

definition: The decision to stop searching follows declared coverage and marginal-yield rules.
required_evidence: Coverage state, unresolved gaps, marginal yield, stop rule, and decision event.
score_0: Search stops by paper count alone or without evidence.
score_1: A stop reason exists but coverage, yield, or unresolved gaps are incomplete.
score_2: The stop decision is fully supported by coverage, yield, and unresolved-gap evidence.

definition: All studies are compared using the same decision-relevant dimensions.
required_evidence: Comparison matrix with rows for studies and the rubric's required dimensions.
score_0: Studies are only summarized separately or use incompatible dimensions.
score_1: A shared matrix exists but one or more required dimensions are missing or uneven.
score_2: Every study is compared on all applicable required dimensions with missing data explicit.

definition: Every substantive comparison judgment links to verified source evidence.
required_evidence: Comparison cells linked to claim and evidence IDs.
score_0: A central comparison judgment has no source in the evidence packet.
score_1: Most judgments are linked, but central support or locators are incomplete.
score_2: All central comparison judgments link to verified, locatable evidence.

definition: The comparison identifies agreements, disagreements, and incompatible assumptions.
required_evidence: Evidence-backed synthesis of convergent, conflicting, and incomparable results.
score_0: Material conflicts are ignored or false agreement is asserted.
score_1: Some conflicts are named, but assumptions or consequences are incomplete.
score_2: Major agreements, conflicts, and incompatibilities are explicit and evidence-backed.

definition: The comparison explains which conditions make findings or methods change and how that affects the project.
required_evidence: Condition-by-result links and recorded downstream design decisions.
score_0: Condition-dependent evidence is treated as universal or has no design consequence.
score_1: Relevant conditions are named but effects or downstream decisions are incomplete.
score_2: Condition effects are evidence-backed and explicitly change the downstream research decision.

definition: Each proposed direction identifies and accurately represents its closest existing work.
required_evidence: Direction-to-work links and dimension-by-dimension similarity comparison.
score_0: No closest work is identified or it is materially misrepresented.
score_1: A plausible closest work is named but verification or comparison is incomplete.
score_2: The nearest verified work is accurately compared on all contribution-relevant dimensions.

definition: Each direction separates what evidence already establishes from what remains unknown.
required_evidence: Claim ledger labeled established, uncertain, conflicting, or missing.
score_0: Known findings are called gaps or missing evidence is called established.
score_1: The separation is plausible but one or more central claims remain ambiguous.
score_2: Established, uncertain, conflicting, and missing claims are distinctly evidence-backed.

definition: Each gap states the population, place, period, behavior, mechanism, and evidence limits where it applies.
required_evidence: Explicit scope fields and evidence supporting each boundary.
score_0: The gap is universal, vague, or outside the reviewed evidence.
score_1: Some scope limits exist but one or more decision-critical boundaries are absent.
score_2: All material gap boundaries are explicit and supported by the reviewed evidence.

definition: Each direction states the exact new evidence, method, or capability added beyond closest work.
required_evidence: Before/after contribution statement tied to closest-work limitations.
score_0: The proposed work duplicates closest work or states only a topic.
score_1: A possible increment exists but novelty, deliverable, or comparison is incomplete.
score_2: The increment is specific, non-duplicative, and directly tied to a verified limitation.

definition: Each gap states what new evidence would weaken or remove the claimed opportunity.
required_evidence: Disconfirming evidence condition and the decision it would change.
score_0: No falsifier exists or the gap is framed as impossible to disconfirm.
score_1: A falsifier is mentioned but is not observable or linked to a decision.
score_2: A concrete observable result would clearly weaken the gap and alter the decision.

definition: Every part of the gap statement can be traced to comparison evidence and source claims.
required_evidence: Gap components linked to comparison cells, claims, and evidence IDs.
score_0: A central gap component has no evidence trace.
score_1: Most components are traceable, but at least one central link is incomplete.
score_2: All central gap components are traceable through comparison to verified evidence.

definition: The direction would change knowledge or a real research decision for a named audience.
required_evidence: Audience, decision, expected knowledge change, and supporting rationale.
score_0: No meaningful audience or decision is affected.
score_1: Potential value exists but audience, decision, or magnitude is vague.
score_2: A named audience faces a clear decision or knowledge gain supported by evidence.

definition: The direction's contribution is meaningfully larger than a cosmetic variation on closest work.
required_evidence: Closest-work comparison and concrete contribution delta.
score_0: The direction duplicates prior work or changes only presentation.
score_1: A contribution exists but its importance or uniqueness is uncertain.
score_2: The contribution is specific, material, and verified against closest work.

definition: Required data are identifiable, accessible, licensed, and sufficient for the proposed analysis.
required_evidence: Dataset names, access route, variables, coverage, license, and limitations.
score_0: Critical data are unavailable or assumed without evidence.
score_1: Likely data exist but access, variables, license, or sufficiency is unresolved.
score_2: All critical data have verified access, variables, coverage, and permitted use.

definition: The direction can be tested against evidence independent of calibration or prompting.
required_evidence: Validation targets, holdouts, metrics, and independence rationale.
score_0: No credible independent validation target exists.
score_1: A target exists but independence, metric, or coverage is incomplete.
score_2: Credible independent targets and metrics can test the direction's central claims.

definition: The direction fits the team's 16-week skills, dependencies, and ordinary computing resources.
required_evidence: Task estimates, owners, dependencies, resource bounds, and critical path.
score_0: A critical dependency makes the direction infeasible with no alternative.
score_1: The plan is plausible but key estimates, owners, or dependencies are uncertain.
score_2: The scoped direction fits the stated team, schedule, and resource bounds.

definition: Major scientific and execution risks each have a trigger and workable fallback.
required_evidence: Risk register with probability, impact, trigger, owner, and fallback.
score_0: A likely critical risk has no fallback.
score_1: Risks and fallbacks exist but triggers, owners, or viability are incomplete.
score_2: Every major risk has a monitored trigger, owner, and executable fallback.

definition: The recommended direction follows the same declared criteria used for every alternative and remains a human-recorded choice.
required_evidence: Scored comparison, tradeoff rationale, and human decision event.
score_0: The recommendation is arbitrary or uses hidden criteria.
score_1: Alternatives are compared but weighting, tradeoffs, or the decision record is incomplete.
score_2: The same criteria support a transparent tradeoff and an explicit human decision.

definition: The study declares confirmatory, exploratory, method-development, or simulation-discovery mode and follows that mode's obligations.
required_evidence: Mode declaration, rationale, and mode-specific required fields.
score_0: Mode is absent, inconsistent, or exploratory output is labeled confirmatory.
score_1: A mode is declared but one or more required obligations are incomplete.
score_2: The declared mode is justified and every mode-specific obligation is satisfied.

definition: The study states either a testable estimand or a bounded exploratory target with units and outcomes.
required_evidence: Estimand fields or exploration space, unit, outcome, pattern, and multiplicity rules.
score_0: The target is undefined, unobservable, or changes after results without a record.
score_1: A target exists but units, comparisons, outcomes, or multiplicity rules are incomplete.
score_2: The target is observable, bounded, reproducible, and appropriate to the declared mode.

definition: Observed or projected demographic states map reproducibly to agent attributes, populations, or weights.
required_evidence: Variable mapping, synthesis or weighting method, constraints, and provenance.
score_0: The mapping is missing or demographic attributes are invented without support.
score_1: A plausible mapping exists but variables, weights, constraints, or provenance are incomplete.
score_2: Every demographic input maps reproducibly to agent states or weights with provenance.

definition: Aggregated consumer outcomes update later environments or agent states through empirically governed rules.
required_evidence: Feedback variables, update equations or rules, lag, bounds, and empirical source.
score_0: Feedback is absent despite the bidirectional claim or is invented by an LLM as truth.
score_1: A feedback path exists but its empirical rule, lag, or bounds are incomplete.
score_2: Each feedback path is explicit, bounded, empirically governed, and reproducible.

definition: The LLM's observations, allowed choices, output schema, failure handling, and prohibited roles are explicit.
required_evidence: Prompt or policy contract, structured output schema, validation, retries, and guardrails.
score_0: LLM behavior is unconstrained or supplies demographic ground truth.
score_1: The LLM role is mostly specified but choices, failures, or prohibited uses are incomplete.
score_2: Inputs, choices, outputs, failures, and prohibited roles are fully specified and testable.

definition: Within-period order, cross-period state changes, lags, and termination are explicit.
required_evidence: State-transition schedule, clocks, lag rules, initialization, and stopping condition.
score_0: Time order is undefined or creates circular updates with no resolution.
score_1: A schedule exists but at least one state, lag, or termination rule is ambiguous.
score_2: All state updates, lags, initialization, and stopping rules are deterministic or logged.

definition: Individual choices aggregate to population outcomes using declared weights and uncertainty rules.
required_evidence: Aggregation equations, weights, estimators, uncertainty, and missing-data handling.
score_0: Aggregation is missing or incompatible with the agent population.
score_1: Aggregation exists but weighting, uncertainty, or missing-data treatment is incomplete.
score_2: Aggregation is reproducible and aligned with population weights and uncertainty.

definition: Conclusions stay within the simulation design, evidence, and identified causal or descriptive scope.
required_evidence: Claim-to-design matrix and explicit prohibited interpretations.
score_0: A conditional simulation is stated as an observed real-world causal effect.
score_1: Most claims are bounded but one or more causal, population, or temporal limits are vague.
score_2: Every central claim is explicitly bounded by the design and supporting evidence.

definition: The synthetic or reweighted population matches independent demographic targets.
required_evidence: Holdout demographic margins or microstructure targets and discrepancy metrics.
score_0: Population fit is untested or checked only on construction inputs.
score_1: Some independent margins are tested but important structure or holdout separation is incomplete.
score_2: Independent targets test both key margins and relevant joint population structure.

definition: Agent consumption choices are compared with credible observed or experimental behavior.
required_evidence: Behavioral targets, matched contexts, metrics, and uncertainty intervals.
score_0: Choices are judged only by plausibility or another LLM.
score_1: Observed targets exist but context matching, metrics, or coverage is incomplete.
score_2: Independent behavioral data test the main decisions in matched contexts with uncertainty.

definition: The direction and magnitude of feedback dynamics are tested against empirical or accepted structural targets.
required_evidence: Time-series, elasticity, transition, or structural targets plus dynamic error metrics.
score_0: Feedback is never tested or is validated by the same rule used to create it.
score_1: Some dynamic targets exist but direction, magnitude, lag, or independence is incomplete.
score_2: Independent evidence tests feedback direction, magnitude, lag, and stability.

definition: Aggregate and distributional consumption outcomes match independent real-world targets within stated tolerance.
required_evidence: Holdout outcome distributions, moments, subgroup results, and error metrics.
score_0: Only aggregate plausibility is shown or no real target exists.
score_1: Some outcomes are tested but distributions, subgroups, tolerance, or holdout coverage is incomplete.
score_2: Independent aggregate and distributional targets are tested with declared tolerances.

definition: Calibration inputs and final validation targets are separate and recorded before evaluation.
required_evidence: Dataset split, time or population split, hashes, and permitted uses.
score_0: Calibration data are reused and reported as independent validation.
score_1: A split is intended but leakage controls or hashes are incomplete.
score_2: Calibration and holdout evidence are predeclared, disjoint, hashed, and leakage-checked.

definition: A transparent non-LLM model provides a meaningful lower-complexity comparison.
required_evidence: Baseline specification, identical inputs, evaluation metrics, and results.
score_0: No non-LLM baseline exists where one is feasible.
score_1: A baseline exists but inputs, tuning, or evaluation are not comparable.
score_2: A transparent baseline receives matched inputs and is evaluated on identical metrics.

definition: An unconditioned or reduced-LLM variant identifies what the LLM component adds.
required_evidence: Ablation definition, controlled inputs, repeated results, and effect comparison.
score_0: No ablation exists or LLM underperformance is hidden.
score_1: An ablation exists but controls, repeats, or interpretation are incomplete.
score_2: A controlled ablation isolates the LLM contribution and reports gains or losses.

definition: Every critical dataset has a verified access route, license, format, and expected delivery time.
required_evidence: Access test, license record, variables, format, size, and acquisition date.
score_0: A critical dataset is unavailable or assumed available without evidence.
score_1: Likely access exists but license, variables, format, or timing is unresolved.
score_2: All critical datasets have verified usable access and permitted use.

definition: A minimum viable study answers a useful subset of the question with bounded data, agents, scenarios, and outputs.
required_evidence: MVP scope, success criteria, excluded features, and expansion path.
score_0: The minimum plan is still too large or cannot answer a useful question.
score_1: An MVP exists but boundaries or success criteria are incomplete.
score_2: The MVP is executable, decision-useful, and explicitly bounded.

definition: The 16-week plan has tasks, owners, dependencies, milestones, and slack.
required_evidence: Week-by-week plan, critical path, decision dates, and owner assignments.
score_0: The critical path cannot fit 16 weeks.
score_1: A schedule exists but owners, dependencies, gates, or slack are incomplete.
score_2: The complete critical path fits 16 weeks with owners, gates, and contingency time.

definition: Compute, LLM calls, runtime, and monetary cost are measured or conservatively bounded.
required_evidence: Workload assumptions, call counts, token or runtime estimates, prices, and sensitivity range.
score_0: Unknown usage is recorded as zero or required resources exceed constraints.
score_1: Estimates exist but assumptions, range, or measurement plan is incomplete.
score_2: All material resources are measured or bounded with assumptions and sensitivity ranges.

definition: Predeclared checkpoints determine whether to continue, revise, reduce scope, or stop.
required_evidence: Gate date, required evidence, threshold, decision owner, and allowed actions.
score_0: No gate exists before an irreversible or costly dependency.
score_1: Gates exist but thresholds, evidence, owners, or actions are incomplete.
score_2: Every critical dependency has an evidence-based gate and recorded decision owner.

definition: Scientific, data, implementation, model, cost, and schedule risks are monitored.
required_evidence: Risk register with likelihood, impact, signal, owner, and update date.
score_0: A critical known risk is omitted.
score_1: Major risks are listed but signals, owners, or updates are incomplete.
score_2: All material risk classes are monitored with explicit signals and owners.

definition: Every critical risk has a smaller executable alternative that preserves research value.
required_evidence: Fallback trigger, reduced design, required assets, expected claim, and switch cost.
score_0: A critical failure leaves no executable study.
score_1: Fallbacks are named but feasibility or preserved value is unclear.
score_2: Each critical failure has a tested or evidence-backed fallback with a valid claim boundary.

definition: A central source is fabricated or its identity is materially mismatched.
A central DOI or version resolves to another work.
A central method or finding contradicts its cited source.
An unsupported universal absence claim is used to establish novelty.
An exploratory finding is presented as confirmatory evidence.
Incomplete verification is reported as verified.
Obvious closest work is omitted while novelty is claimed.
Keyword-only material is counted as verified cluster coverage.
Benchmark titles enter production queries or stopping logic.
A backend failure is recorded as a valid empty result.
A decision history is overwritten.
A missing artifact is reported as verified.
Methods with incompatible units or assumptions are declared equivalent.
A central comparison judgment relies on a source absent from the evidence packet.
The direction claims no prior study exists without adequate evidence.
Closest work is materially misrepresented.
A literature-search omission is presented as novelty.
A direction is recommended using a criterion not applied to alternatives.
Known data or validation infeasibility is omitted.
An exploratory pattern is presented as confirmatory evidence.
An LLM invents demographic transitions treated as observed truth.
A conditional simulation result is stated as a real-world causal effect.
The named method conflicts with its actual state, time, interaction, or weighting structure.
Calibration data are reported as independent validation.
Judge preference is the only behavioral ground truth.
LLM underperformance is hidden or excluded from the result.
Unknown cost or usage is recorded as zero.
Private or restricted data are assumed available without evidence.
A large-scale design is called feasible without a bounded MVP.
